- Integration with Spring).  This merge was done before the migration to git, so its history is not immediately available.  At least we now know where to look, though

Rebuilder does eventually terminate after one minute if left to wait.  This wait is independent on rebuild task (db vs triplestore), or database impl.   Inspecting thread state does not point to an obvious culprit

I'm seeing the same behavior here, with embedded Derby. I also noticed that when exiting via option 4, I get a NPE and the app hangs indefinitely (doesn't exit after a minute like it does when you run a rebuild). Maybe related, maybe not.

It turns out that adding a System.exit(0) after normal execution (and a System.exit(1) after failed execution) in the rebuilder's main() method prevents this delay.
Just an update...I verified that NotificationInvocationHandler is
the cause of this issue; the Management module does
get started as part of the rebuilder.

Another tidbit: I used jdb to determine that when the rebuilder first starts, the thread named "pool-1-thread-1" does not exist. Only after requesting a rebuild be run is it created. I think I can use this fact to zero in on how this thread comes into existence through a series of strategically placed thread dumps...

So far, using strategically placed thread dumps, I've narrowed down the creation of pool-1-thread-1 to somewhere in the execution of FOXMLDODeserializer.deserialize. It exists after the first time that method is called from within Rebuild.addObject, and doesn't go away on its own. Hmm.

I've now narrowed it (the creation of pool-1-thread-1) down to somewhere in org.fcrepo.server.storage.RDFRelationshipReader#readRelationships. This is basically a thin wrapper around some calls to Trippi, which ultimately uses RIOTripleIterator to parse the stream of triples. RIOTripleIterator has historically used a separate thread to parse the triples. Looking at recent changes to Trippi, I see

...which switched to using a java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService (thread pool) instead of spinning up a thread itself. However, the EXECUTOR field is final static, and only typed as an Executor, which doesn't have a shutdown() method like ExecutorService does. Therefore, ExecutorService.shutdown() can never possibly be called.
Now I'm pretty sure this is the cause, because the javadoc for Executors.newCachedThreadPool()[1] says:
"Threads that have not been used for sixty seconds are terminated and removed from the cache."
Attached demo maven project to reproduce the hang by calling Trippi's TripleIterator.fromStream method, when RIOTripleIterator is used. See README in zip file for instructions.
Fixed in Trippi 1.5.2 by moving back to a thread-per-parse model. See
If you change the trippi version to 1.5.2 in the attached project's pom, you'll see that it exits immediately now.
Just a note that the final fix for this was the same as that for FCREPO-873. See
After rebuilder finishes, it does not exit on its own.  It appears to freeze until ^C

It turns out that adding a System.exit(0) after normal execution (and a System.exit(1) after failed execution) in the rebuilder's main() method prevents this delay.
Just an update...I verified that NotificationInvocationHandler is not the cause of this issue; the Management module does not get started as part of the rebuilder.

Another tidbit: I used jdb to determine that when the rebuilder first starts, the thread named "pool-1-thread-1" does not exist. Only after requesting a rebuild be run is it created. I think I can use this fact to zero in on how this thread comes into existence through a series of strategically placed thread dumps...

So far, using strategically placed thread dumps, I've narrowed down the creation of pool-1-thread-1 to somewhere in the execution of FOXMLDODeserializer.deserialize. It exists after the first time that method is called from within Rebuild.addObject, and doesn't go away on its own. Hmm.

I've now narrowed it (the creation of pool-1-thread-1) down to somewhere in org.fcrepo.server.storage.RDFRelationshipReader#readRelationships. This is basically a thin wrapper around some calls to Trippi, which ultimately uses RIOTripleIterator to parse the stream of triples. RIOTripleIterator has historically used a separate thread to parse the triples. Looking at recent changes to Trippi, I see https://github.com/fcrepo/trippi/commit/62b0725f7abc1d7517566d8dfdbf763516d2f81c ...which switched to using a java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService (thread pool) instead of spinning up a thread itself. However, the EXECUTOR field is final static, and only typed as an Executor, which doesn't have a shutdown() method like ExecutorService does. Therefore, ExecutorService.shutdown() can never possibly be called.

Now I'm pretty sure this is the cause, because the javadoc for Executors.newCachedThreadPool()[1] says:

"Threads that have not been used for sixty seconds are terminated and removed from the cache."

[1] http://download.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/Executors.html#newCachedThreadPool%28%29
Attached demo maven project to reproduce the hang by calling Trippi's TripleIterator.fromStream method, when RIOTripleIterator is used. See README in zip file for instructions.

Fixed in Trippi 1.5.2 by moving back to a thread-per-parse model. See https://github.com/fcrepo/trippi/commit/4ef40ea22b4a6b359de73c4b4d8b5a9fe432a594

If you change the trippi version to 1.5.2 in the attached project's pom, you'll see that it exits immediately now.

Just a note that the final fix for this was the same as that for FCREPO-873 Closed . See https://github.com/fcrepo/trippi/commit/eed9d49fe9b03e3e18658c8c8804ee37a415d169 https://github.com/fcrepo/trippi/commit/229cf6a71f7705c57a097b19fa6397762392b656 and https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/commit/391bc9af8544bcb1033b01311db7d0f5ade0d05d
